returned.how_to_read: If the holder's own prior transactions are confirmed fraud, this holder identity is compromised: matching its baseline is evidence FOR fraud, not against it. A holder is defined by card, billing region and anchor day, so its history is always in its own region: whether the region is new can only be read at card level (alert_context.card_history.flagged_region_share_of_card).

lift = share of transactions on this element scoring >= 0.5, divided by the same share across all transactions. Large regions and common email domains carry many unrelated cards; a shared origin needs lift well above 1 and several distinct cards.

Card C12223-K1 is in community 121635001 with a fraud lift of 5.0, but this is a 2-card community whose elevated rate is driven entirely by the card's own historical case CC-0179 rather than links to external fraudsters.

Although the card was linked to a prior compromise in July 2016 (CC-0179), the card was subsequently reissued, and the current holder profile has no confirmed fraud history. The alert is confirmed as a false alarm and the case is closed as legitimate.
